title: From Nagoya to Adelaide (1)
paragraphs: From the end of February 2016, I stayed for about one month as a summer student in a laboratory at the University of Adelaide in South Australia. It all began in November 2015. I wanted to use my spring vacation for something that would be useful for my future. At first, I looked into studying abroad with the idea of "studying English." However, I came to think that "if possible, I would like to experience actual research abroad rather than a language course." When I consulted Dr. 豊國伸哉 of the Department of Pathology and Biological Responses, who had taught me in the basic medicine seminar in my third year, he said that the University of Adelaide, a partner university of Nagoya University, might be able to accept me. I was very fortunate that he contacted Dr. Ossama right away, things went smoothly, and this stay in Adelaide became a reality. I chose the laboratory of Professor Christine Feinle-Bisset at the University of Adelaide as my host. The reason was that I really wanted to see how nutrition research is carried out. For the one-month stay, a program was arranged in which I took part in various studies as an observer and listened to many researchers. Most of the studies involved giving a medical intervention (such as pre-meal protein administration through a nasal tube) to healthy volunteers or volunteers with type 2 diabetes, and observing changes in hunger and hormone dynamics through interviews and blood sampling. It was a pity that I could not learn concrete results, since it takes from half a year to several years for a single study to become a paper, but it was educational to see in person the research methods commonly used in nutrition research. In the past, when I read accounts saying "I grew through studying abroad," I wondered whether it was really true. However, now that I have actually finished my time abroad, I truly feel that I have grown. To the people around me, it may seem that I merely stayed in Australia for a month. But for me, it was a very precious experience that changed me. There are almost no Japanese people in Adelaide, so I had no choice but to speak English. Spending a month in such an environment gave me great confidence. Around the University of Adelaide there are museums, art galleries, a zoo and a botanical garden, and in the suburbs there are well-equipped shopping malls and beaches, so it is full of attractions. The city is full of nature, the buildings are beautiful, and the people are sociable, so it was a wonderful place. Although it was a short period, through this study abroad I have become able to picture my future more clearly. I deeply thank Dr. 豊國 who strongly encouraged me to study abroad despite his busy schedule, Dr. 粕谷 and Dr. Ossama who gave me advice on studying abroad, Professor Christine who kindly accepted an inexperienced person like me, Dr. Penelope who arranged the program during my stay and looked after me every day, Dr. Christiane who gave me advice about the stay and showed me around the campus, and everyone who helped me there.
